title: EF Core & SQL — N+1, indexes, AsNoTracking
exp: Data access is where mid-senior candidates separate themselves: N+1, plans, and read vs write patterns.
pts: N+1: fix with `Include`, projections, split queries, or Dapper joins.
Indexes: clustered vs nonclustered; seek vs scan; covering `INCLUDE`.
`AsNoTracking()` for read-only lists — less memory, faster.
Change tracker identity resolution: same key → same instance.
Know how to read a basic execution plan in interviews.
code:
var orders = await db.Orders
    .AsNoTracking()
    .Include(o => o.Items)
    .Where(o => o.CustomerId == id)
    .ToListAsync(ct);
pr: Rewrite an N+1 loop with Include + projection
Propose an index for a slow WHERE/ORDER BY

qa.q: What is the N+1 problem and how do you fix it in EF?
qa.a: Loading a collection then lazy-loading a navigation per row causes 1+N queries. Fix with Include/ThenInclude, Select projections, AsSplitQuery for big graphs, or explicit SQL joins. Verify with logging or a profiler.
Read-only queries where you won't Update/SaveChanges. Skipping tracking reduces memory and CPU. Don't use it if you need to mutate and persist the same instances.
